method: Web research via WebFetch + WebSearch (subagent), all citations primary

external_audit.opinion_detail: Audit of 2024/25 accounts commenced 4 August 2025 following July 2025 planning activities. Fieldwork underway. Scheduled to complete by end of December 2025 with audit findings to Audit and Risk Assurance Committee 15 January 2026 and final SoA published by 30 January 2026. Backstop deadline for 2024/25 was 27 February 2026. Prior years 2022/23 and 2023/24 received DISCLAIMER OF OPINION by Grant Thornton due to backstop time constraints, NOT due to underlying control failures - explicitly noted in cabinet paper as the auditor unable to gain assurance necessary by backstop date.
external_audit.vfm_conclusion: 2024/25 VfM work in progress. 2021 Grant Thornton VfM Governance Review identified three statutory recommendations - all three LIFTED by Grant Thornton December 2023 follow-up review.
key_risks_in_2024_25_audit_plan: Valuation of land and buildings, council dwellings and investment properties
Valuation of pension fund net liability
Implementation of Oracle Fusion General Ledger (post-implementation review needed)
VfM risk: delivery of housing service - Housing Improvement and Transformation Programme being monitored
VfM risk: Sandwell Childrens Trust £3M deterioration vs forecast outturn (control weakness concern)

commissioners: Kim Bromley-Derry CBE DL (lead, also interim CEO from August 2021)
historical_intervention.trigger: Grant Thornton VfM Governance Review 3 December 2021 identified deeply troubling picture of mismanagement and ineffective scrutiny and accountability arrangements
historical_intervention.sos_finding: Secretary of State agreed Council now meeting Best Value Duty; Commissioners fourth report 7 March 2024 concluded Council ready to move forward without Commissioner support

internal_audit.overall_opinion_detail: In the opinion of Internal Audit, reasonable assurance could be provided that the Council had adequate and effective governance, risk management and internal control processes. Opinion based on work undertaken throughout the year by Internal Audit alongside work by other external bodies. Audits conducted in accordance with Public Sector Internal Audit Standards. Majority of key financial systems work undertaken during SBS-to-Oracle Fusion transition (which temporarily increased audit issues raised and recommendations made).
limited_assurance_subjects: Aids and adaptations - delays in equipping households with required adaptations to support independent living
Use of council procurement cards - follow-up review showed slight improvement; further tightened controls required for transaction documentation
Accounts receivable and capital accounting - discrepancies identified in data transferred between SBS and Oracle Fusion (raised with Oracle Fusion Support team)
Sandwell Community School - governance and financial controls concerns; recommendations made to strengthen arrangements and terms of reference
Fifth subject not enumerated in extracted September 2025 committee minutes - check full Internal Audit Annual Report

mtfs_2026_31.title: Draft MTFS 2026/27 to 2030/31
mtfs_2026_31.reserves_strategy: Council has enhanced reserves strategy introduced in 2025/26. MTFS does not factor in use of General Reserves in medium term to balance financial deficits from 2027/28 onwards. 2026/27 includes -£19.792M draw to offset Sandwell Childrens Trust cumulative deficit (over 3 years), -£2.640M dividend receipts to balance, -£0.180M to fund Sandwell Plan document.

strategic_risks.register_status: Live register maintained by Audit and Risk Assurance Committee; status reported in May 2025 meeting and ongoing
red_risks_may_2025: Demand and cost of SEND Placements and Transport
mtfs_strategic_risks: Childrens Social Care - if Sandwell Childrens Trust does not address performance issues, risks failing statutory responsibilities
Compliance with Data Protection Act 2018, GDPR and Freedom of Information Act 2000
Regeneration Fund Programmes - delivery to scope, time and budget
Equalities - failure to meet Equality Act 2010 / Public Sector Equality Duty obligations

dsg_send.dsg_reserve_status_2025_26: High Needs Block reserve position becoming a deficit reserve in 2025/26 - estimated £4.167M negative balance held against overall council resources, not chargeable to General Fund under statutory override
dsg_send.safety_valve_status: Not in Safety Valve programme; per MTFS, working on mitigation strategy via strategic partner for 12-month SEND transformation programme (strategy and forward planning, locality model, SEND service restructure, front door model for Inclusive Learning Services, whole school SEND/inclusion offer, home to school transport review)
dsg_send.sandwell_childrens_trust_remediation: Council intends to resolve Trust deficit by drawing £19.792M from earmarked reserves; new 3-year contract sum 2025/26-2027/28 funded from reserves of £6.597M in 2026/27 and 2027/28 to reduce deficit to nil over period

asc_market_sustainability.plan_published: not located via web search - check sandwell.gov.uk publications
asc_market_sustainability.asc_pressure_driver: Inflation associated with Adult Social Care contracts and increase from April 2026 in National Living Wage; £10.328M ongoing growth from 2026/27 for inflationary pressures + £7.404M ongoing budget growth for ASC placements
asc_market_sustainability.follow_up_required: Verify Market Sustainability Plan publication on sandwell.gov.uk

lgr.context: Sandwell is a metropolitan borough within the West Midlands Combined Authority (WMCA). No live LGR consultation for West Midlands metropolitan boroughs.

property_strategy.name: General Fund Capital Programme (MTFS Annex 9)
property_strategy.capital_debt_service_pct_target: Below 6% of council net budget for MTFS period (currently 6%)

actionable_savings_levers_summary: Cumulative £155M budget gap pre-efficiency over 5 years (2026/27 to 2030/31) with only £45.5M efficiencies identified - £109M remaining unidentified gap
Sandwell Childrens Trust £19.792M cumulative deficit being absorbed by reserves over 3 years - performance/cost reduction critical to avoid further drawdown
DSG High Needs Block deficit just starting (£4.167M in 25/26) - early Safety Valve engagement could prevent Lancashire-scale £243M trajectory

Oracle Fusion General Ledger post-implementation review is auditor priority - cleanup of SBS-to-Fusion data discrepancies, accounts receivable and capital accounting (limited-assurance internal audit subjects)
Counter-fraud: £3.37M recovered/prevented in 2024/25 against 194 investigations - scope to extend SPD fraud programme (£73k removed via 134 penalty notices)
Procurement card controls remain limited-assurance - follow-up internal audit needed to confirm full remediation
Housing Improvement and Transformation Programme is auditor VfM monitoring item - delivery progress directly affects audit risk rating
